question: What is market failure? Explain the main reasons why markets fail.
sources: Market failure and the role of government (standard public finance / welfare economics)

points.label: Meaning
points.description: Market failure is a situation where free markets, left alone, do not allocate resources efficiently, so social welfare is not maximised.

points.label: Market power
points.description: Monopoly or other market power lets firms restrict output and charge prices above marginal cost.

points.label: Externalities
points.description: Externalities are costs or benefits that fall on third parties and are not reflected in prices, such as pollution (negative) or vaccination (positive); goods with negative externalities are over-produced and those with positive ones under-produced.

points.label: Public goods
points.description: Public goods are non-rival and non-excludable, so people can enjoy them without paying (free-rider problem) and markets under-supply them.

points.label: Incomplete information
points.description: When buyers or sellers lack information, or one side knows more than the other (asymmetric information), problems like adverse selection and moral hazard arise.
points.basis: Market failure: incomplete and asymmetric information
